quests.hint: Confirming that a theory or idea is actually correct, often through testing.
quests.explanation: 'Validate a theory' is common in research and business. The noun form is 'validation.'
quests.textToSpeak: The pilot results helped ___ her theory, giving her the confidence to expand the program.
quests.correctAnswer: The pilot results helped validate her theory, giving her the confidence to expand the program.

quests.hint: Continuing to maintain and support a high standard, even under pressure.
quests.explanation: 'Uphold standards' is a common phrase in workplace values. It can also mean supporting a decision or tradition already in place.
quests.textToSpeak: The company has always tried to ___ the highest standards of customer service, even during difficult years.
quests.correctAnswer: The company has always tried to uphold the highest standards of customer service, even during difficult years.

quests.hint: Publicly and persistently fighting for a cause you believe in.
quests.explanation: 'Champion a cause' uses the word as a verb, not just a noun for a winner. It suggests years of consistent advocacy.
quests.textToSpeak: She has spent her whole career trying to ___ better rights for part-time workers.
quests.correctAnswer: She has spent her whole career trying to champion better rights for part-time workers.

quests.hint: Showing itself clearly, often through physical or visible signs.
quests.explanation: 'Manifest itself in' is the natural choice here. As an adjective, manifest also means obvious or clear.
quests.textToSpeak: Stress can ___ itself in surprising ways, like headaches or trouble sleeping.
quests.correctAnswer: Stress can manifest itself in surprising ways, like headaches or trouble sleeping.

quests.hint: The real, deeper cause hidden beneath the surface of a problem.
quests.explanation: 'An underlying issue' is what's actually causing a problem, even if it's not immediately obvious.
quests.textToSpeak: There's clearly an ___ issue here that we haven't fully addressed yet.
quests.correctAnswer: There's clearly an underlying issue here that we haven't fully addressed yet.

quests.hint: Something that sets off a strong reaction or starts a chain of events.
quests.explanation: 'Trigger a reaction' works as a verb here. As a noun, 'a trigger' can also describe part of a gun, in a different context.
quests.textToSpeak: Nobody could quite identify what would ___ such a strong reaction in him.
quests.correctAnswer: Nobody could quite identify what would trigger such a strong reaction in him.

quests.hint: Formally ending a partnership or organisation.
quests.explanation: 'Dissolve a partnership' is the version people actually use. It can also describe something physically disappearing, like sugar dissolving in tea.
quests.textToSpeak: When the two co-founders fell out, they had no choice but to ___ the partnership.
quests.correctAnswer: When the two co-founders fell out, they had no choice but to dissolve the partnership.

quests.hint: Putting off a decision until a calmer or more suitable moment.
quests.explanation: 'Defer a decision' is common in both business and everyday life. 'Deferred' is the adjective form — 'a deferred payment.'
quests.textToSpeak: Rather than argue in the moment, she decided to ___ the decision until everyone had calmed down.
quests.correctAnswer: Rather than argue in the moment, she decided to defer the decision until everyone had calmed down.

quests.hint: Actually carrying out a plan, not just designing it.
quests.explanation: 'Execute a plan' or 'execute an idea' both work. It's a stronger, more formal word than simply 'do' or 'carry out.'
quests.textToSpeak: The new manager was excellent at planning but struggled to actually ___ her ideas.
quests.correctAnswer: The new manager was excellent at planning but struggled to actually execute her ideas.

quests.hint: Deep, specialised knowledge and skill built up in one particular area.
quests.explanation: 'Expertise in' something is the one to remember. It's uncountable, so we never say 'an expertise' or 'expertises.'
quests.textToSpeak: Her ___ in data analysis made her the obvious choice to lead the project.
quests.correctAnswer: Her expertise in data analysis made her the obvious choice to lead the project.

quests.hint: The qualifications and experience that prove you're right for a role.
quests.explanation: 'The right credentials' is a common phrase. It's almost always used in the plural, even for one person's set of qualifications.
quests.textToSpeak: He had all the right ___ on paper, but the interview didn't go well at all.
quests.correctAnswer: He had all the right credentials on paper, but the interview didn't go well at all.

quests.hint: Careful, tactful judgment about what to say and do in a sensitive situation.
quests.explanation: 'Handle with discretion' means with real tact and care. 'Use your discretion' means trusting your own careful judgment.
quests.textToSpeak: Handling the layoffs required real ___; the manager had to be both honest and kind.
quests.correctAnswer: Handling the layoffs required real discretion; the manager had to be both honest and kind.

quests.hint: Believable enough that people accept it without much doubt.
quests.explanation: 'Sound credible' is what you'll hear most often. Its opposite is 'dubious' or 'implausible.'
quests.textToSpeak: Her explanation for being late seemed pretty ___, so nobody questioned it.
quests.correctAnswer: Her explanation for being late seemed pretty credible, so nobody questioned it.

quests.hint: Refusing to take something seriously and brushing it aside.
quests.explanation: 'Dismiss a concern' is common in workplace discussions. It's a stronger word than simply 'ignore.'
quests.textToSpeak: It would be a mistake to ___ his concerns just because he's new to the team.
quests.correctAnswer: It would be a mistake to dismiss his concerns just because he's new to the team.

quests.hint: So critical and revealing that it seriously damages someone's reputation.
quests.explanation: 'A damning report' is strong criticism, often based on solid evidence. It comes from the same root as 'condemn.'
quests.textToSpeak: The internal report was ___, revealing failures at every level of management.
quests.correctAnswer: The internal report was damning, revealing failures at every level of management.

quests.hint: Having real power to shape opinions or decisions.
quests.explanation: 'One of the most influential voices' is common praise in journalism and culture. The noun form is 'influence.'
quests.textToSpeak: She has become one of the most ___ voices in the industry over the past decade.
quests.correctAnswer: She has become one of the most influential voices in the industry over the past decade.

quests.hint: Something remarkable enough to attract huge, widespread attention.
quests.explanation: 'A global phenomenon' is common for describing huge cultural success. The plural is 'phenomena' — an irregular Greek-origin plural.
quests.textToSpeak: The show became a global ___, translated into more than thirty languages.
quests.correctAnswer: The show became a global phenomenon, translated into more than thirty languages.

quests.hint: Widely accepted and popular, no longer niche or unusual.
quests.explanation: 'Become completely mainstream' describes something moving from niche to widely popular. Its opposite is 'niche' or 'underground.'
quests.textToSpeak: Ten years ago, this kind of music was niche; now it's completely ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Ten years ago, this kind of music was niche; now it's completely mainstream.

quests.hint: So clearly worded that only one interpretation is possible.
quests.explanation: 'Made fully unambiguous' is common in legal and formal writing. Its opposite is 'ambiguous,' open to more than one meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: The terms of the agreement were made fully ___ to avoid any future misunderstanding.
quests.correctAnswer: The terms of the agreement were made fully unambiguous to avoid any future misunderstanding.

quests.hint: Something left out, especially when it should have been included.
quests.explanation: 'A serious omission' is common when discussing incomplete reports. The verb form is 'omit' — 'to omit a fact.'
quests.textToSpeak: The failure to mention the safety risks was a serious ___ from the original report.
quests.correctAnswer: The failure to mention the safety risks was a serious omission from the original report.

quests.hint: A statement known to be untrue, told deliberately.
quests.explanation: 'Repeat a known falsehood' is a formal way of saying 'lie.' It sounds more measured and precise in serious writing.
quests.textToSpeak: The politician was accused of repeating a known ___ in order to mislead the public.
quests.correctAnswer: The politician was accused of repeating a known falsehood in order to mislead the public.

quests.hint: Personally responsible and answerable for the outcome of your actions.
quests.explanation: 'Feel accountable for' is the everyday way to say it. The noun form is 'accountability.'
quests.textToSpeak: As team leader, she felt personally ___ for the missed deadline.
quests.correctAnswer: As team leader, she felt personally accountable for the missed deadline.

quests.hint: Being watched and examined extremely closely by others.
quests.explanation: 'Come under scrutiny' or 'intense scrutiny' are the go-to phrases. The verb form is 'scrutinise.'
quests.textToSpeak: The company's spending came under intense ___ after the report was published.
quests.correctAnswer: The company's spending came under intense scrutiny after the report was published.

quests.hint: Finally proven right after being doubted or criticised for a long time.
quests.explanation: 'Feel vindicated' is common after being proven correct. The noun form is 'vindication.'
quests.textToSpeak: When the results came in, she finally felt ___ after months of criticism.
quests.correctAnswer: When the results came in, she finally felt vindicated after months of criticism.

quests.hint: Consistently doing the right thing, even when nobody's watching.
quests.explanation: 'A reputation for integrity' is high praise. It comes from the same root as 'integer,' meaning whole and undivided.
quests.textToSpeak: She built her career on a reputation for absolute ___ that everyone respected.
quests.correctAnswer: She built her career on a reputation for absolute integrity that everyone respected.

quests.hint: A core belief that guides your decisions, even at personal cost.
quests.explanation: 'Resign on principle' means quitting because of your values, not for practical reasons — don't confuse it with 'principal,' meaning main.
quests.textToSpeak: She resigned on ___ when asked to misrepresent the data in the official report.
quests.correctAnswer: She resigned on principle when asked to misrepresent the data in the official report.

quests.hint: A clear, official instruction given from above.
quests.explanation: 'Receive a directive' is formal workplace language, stronger and more official than a simple 'request.'
quests.textToSpeak: Staff received a clear ___ requiring all meetings to be conducted in writing.
quests.correctAnswer: Staff received a clear directive requiring all meetings to be conducted in writing.

quests.hint: The moral rules that guide right and wrong behaviour in a profession.
quests.explanation: 'A code of ethics' is standard in professional settings. The adjective form is 'ethical' — 'an ethical decision.'
quests.textToSpeak: Doctors are bound by a strict code of professional ___ that governs their behaviour.
quests.correctAnswer: Doctors are bound by a strict code of professional ethics that governs their behaviour.

quests.hint: The shared attitudes and everyday behaviour that define what it's like to work somewhere.
quests.explanation: 'Company culture' is a phrase you'll hear constantly in modern business, shaped by habits and values, not written rules.
quests.textToSpeak: Building a strong company ___ takes years, but it can be damaged in a single day.
quests.correctAnswer: Building a strong company culture takes years, but it can be damaged in a single day.

quests.hint: The core beliefs that guide what a person or organisation considers important.
quests.explanation: 'Fundamentally different values' is a common reason cited for failed partnerships. It's almost always used in the plural.
quests.textToSpeak: The merger failed partly because the two companies had fundamentally different ___.
quests.correctAnswer: The merger failed partly because the two companies had fundamentally different values.
